title: Linked lists

notes: An empty list is a NULL head.
push_front returns the new head, and main stores it: orders = push_front(orders, ...).
Pushing 103, 102, 101 to the front prints them as 101, 102, 103.
The for loop is the standard walk: start at head, stop at NULL, step with n->next.
The free loop saves next before freeing each node, so it never reads freed memory.

exercises.title: Front, length, free
exercises.prompt: With the Node type and list_to_text given, write three functions. Node *push_front(Node *head, int value): a new node (my_alloc) holding value at the front; return the new head (or the old head if memory runs out). int list_length(const Node *head): how many nodes. void list_free(Node *head): free every node with my_free.

tests.call: ({ static char b[100]; Node *h = NULL; h = push_front(h, 3); h = push_front(h, 2); h = push_front(h, 1); list_to_text(h, b); list_free(h); b; })
tests.name: pushes to the front

tests.call: ({ Node *h = NULL; for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) h = push_front(h, i); int n = list_length(h); list_free(h); n; })
tests.name: length

tests.call: ({ int before = live_allocs; Node *h = NULL; for (int i = 0; i < 50; i++) h = push_front(h, i); list_free(h); live_allocs - before; })
tests.name: frees every node

hints: push_front: Node *n = my_alloc(sizeof *n); n->value = value; n->next = head; return n;
list_length: for (const Node *n = head; n != NULL; n = n->next) count++;
list_free: while (head) { Node *next = head->next; my_free(head); head = next; }

exercises.title: Back and find
exercises.prompt: push_front, list_length and list_free are done for you. Write Node *push_back(Node *head, int value): add a new node at the END and return the head (when the list was empty, the new node is the head). Then write Node *find(Node *head, int value): the first node holding value, or NULL.

tests.call: ({ static char b[100]; Node *h = NULL; h = push_back(h, 4); h = push_back(h, 7); h = push_back(h, 9); list_to_text(h, b); list_free(h); b; })
tests.name: keeps arrival order

tests.call: ({ Node *h = push_back(NULL, 5); int r = h->value * 10 + (h->next == NULL); list_free(h); r; })
tests.name: push onto an empty list
tests.hint_if_fail: If head is NULL, the new node is the whole list: return it.

tests.call: ({ Node *h = NULL; h = push_back(h, 4); h = push_back(h, 7); Node *f = find(h, 7); int r = f != NULL && f->value == 7 && f->next == NULL; list_free(h); r; })
tests.name: finds a value

tests.call: ({ Node *h = NULL; h = push_back(h, 4); Node *f = find(h, 99); list_free(h); f == NULL; })
tests.name: missing value gives NULL

tests.call: ({ Node *h = NULL; h = push_back(h, 3); h = push_back(h, 8); h = push_back(h, 3); int r = find(h, 3) == h; list_free(h); r; })
tests.name: first match wins

hints: push_back: make the node with next = NULL first.
Walk with Node *last = head; while (last->next != NULL) last = last->next; then last->next = n;
find: for (Node *n = head; n != NULL; n = n->next) if (n->value == value) return n; return NULL;

exercises.title: A patient leaves the queue
exercises.prompt: The clinic keeps waiting patients' numbers in a list (push_back, list_length and list_free are given). Write Node *list_remove(Node *head, int value): remove the FIRST node holding value, free it with my_free, and return the head (which changes if the first node was removed). If value isn't there, return the list unchanged.

tests.call: ({ static char b[100]; Node *h = NULL; for (int i = 1; i <= 3; i++) h = push_back(h, i); h = list_remove(h, 2); list_to_text(h, b); list_free(h); b; })
tests.name: remove from the middle

tests.call: ({ static char b[100]; Node *h = NULL; for (int i = 1; i <= 3; i++) h = push_back(h, i); h = list_remove(h, 1); list_to_text(h, b); list_free(h); b; })
tests.name: remove the head
tests.hint_if_fail: When the head goes, return head->next as the new head.

tests.call: ({ int before = live_allocs; Node *h = NULL; for (int i = 1; i <= 3; i++) h = push_back(h, i); h = list_remove(h, 2); int r = live_allocs - before; list_free(h); r; })
tests.name: frees the removed node

tests.call: ({ static char b[100]; Node *h = NULL; for (int i = 1; i <= 3; i++) h = push_back(h, i); h = list_remove(h, 3); list_to_text(h, b); list_free(h); b; })
tests.name: remove the last

tests.call: ({ static char b[100]; Node *h = NULL; for (int i = 1; i <= 3; i++) h = push_back(h, i); h = list_remove(h, 9); list_to_text(h, b); list_free(h); b; })
tests.name: value not there

tests.call: ({ static char b[100]; Node *h = push_back(NULL, 5); h = push_back(h, 5); h = list_remove(h, 5); list_to_text(h, b); list_free(h); b; })
tests.name: only the first match

tests.call: ({ static char b[100]; Node *h = push_back(NULL, 4); h = list_remove(h, 4); h = list_remove(h, 4); list_to_text(h, b); b; })
tests.name: down to empty, then remove again

hints: If head is NULL, return NULL. If head->value matches: save head->next, free head, return the saved next.
Otherwise walk with prev = head while prev->next != NULL, looking at prev->next.
When prev->next->value matches: Node *gone = prev->next; prev->next = gone->next; my_free(gone); return head;

quiz.q: How do you know you've reached the end of a linked list?
quiz.why: The last node points at nothing.

quiz.q: What's wrong with: for (n = head; n != NULL; n = n->next) free(n);
choices: It reads n->next after n has been freed

quiz.q: Someone writes push_front(head, 5); without head = in front. What happens?
choices: The new node is made but lost, so it leaks and the list doesn't change
quiz.why: The function returns the new head; you must store it.

quiz.q: Which is faster to add at the front of: a long array or a linked list?
choices: The linked list: no shifting, just one new node
quiz.why: Pushing to a list's front never moves other items.

quiz.q: Which is better for jumping straight to item 500?
choices: Array: data[500] is one step; a list must walk 500 nodes

cards.a: for (Node *n = head; n != NULL; n = n->next)

explain: Explain how removing a node from the middle of a linked list works, drawing the boxes and arrows in words, with numbers you choose.
